# srdcheck

> Deterministic rules verdicts for game-running agents. Machine adjudication of
> the System Reference Document 5.2.1 (2024 rules, CC-BY-4.0): exit code 0 =
> passes the named checked scope, 1 = conflicts with that scope, 2 =
> cannot-adjudicate (honest refusal — unknown content, DM discretion, or
> genuinely ambiguous rules text). Applied rules carry source quotes; boundary
> refusals do not invent citations. No LLM calls, no network, no
> randomness in the verdict path; p95 single-verdict CI budget under 100 ms;
> MIT.

Use srdcheck for a query listed in `srdcheck capabilities`. Every native verdict
carries `coverage_level`, `checked_scope`, `unchecked_scope`, `assumptions`,
`facts`, `rule_result`, `table_decision`, and `state_mutation`; treat those
per-result fields as the boundary and provenance of the answer. Current examples include
modeled turn budgets, supplied attack modifiers, registered spell facts,
creature registry facts, and supported declared state events. It does not
currently validate multiclass builds or enumerate every creature-specific move.
The calling agent may itself be the authorized DM; its table rulings remain
distinct from SRD-derived results.

For a suite result envelope, add `--table-evaluation` to `query` or `--pipe`.
The deterministic `table.evaluation/1.0` projection is always self_attested;
it preserves self-contained rule/citation evidence and never grants table
authority, including when the caller is an agent-DM. Its subject includes a
machine-readable named-query scope. Add `--table-context` JSON for caller-owned
session/entity/correlation references, or call the opt-in MCP tool
`table_evaluation` with `{query_type, params, context?}`.

On `cannot-adjudicate`, branch on the recovery fields in `data`, never on
`why`: repair the request, provide the named missing facts, select an adapter,
use another capability, resolve a table ruling, or stop.
`required_authority: "dm"` is permission-aware rather than person-aware: an
authorized agent-DM may rule directly, while another caller escalates. See
[docs/refusal-recovery.md](docs/refusal-recovery.md).

Annotate query parameter paths with `asserted_facts` entries containing
`source` and `confidence`; optionally record a scoped `table_decision`. The DM
decision is echoed separately and never rewrites `rule_result`; current queries
explicitly report `state_mutation.status: "none"`. See
[docs/fact-provenance.md](docs/fact-provenance.md).

## Install and first verdict

- CLI: `pip install git+https://github.com/chaoz23/srdcheck` then
  `srdcheck jurisdiction "Fireball"` (exit 0) or
  `srdcheck jurisdiction "Hexblade"` (exit 2, honestly refused).
- MCP (stdio, zero dependencies): command `srdcheck-mcp`; discover the current
  tool count and scope from `srdcheck capabilities`.
- Machine surfaces: [tool.json](tool.json), `srdcheck --schema`.

## Key files

- [README.md](README.md): quickstart, MCP config, truth scorecard.
- [docs/product-truths.md](docs/product-truths.md): the 14 invariants,
  CI-enforced where mechanically possible.
- [docs/anatomy-of-a-turn.md](docs/anatomy-of-a-turn.md): where srdcheck sits
  in an agent-DM pipeline, split into executable-today and target behavior.
- [docs/capability-map.json](docs/capability-map.json): generated checked scope,
  unchecked scope, release tuple, and target claims for agents.
- [docs/adapter-spec.md](docs/adapter-spec.md): rulesets are adapters; the
  kernel contains zero game vocabulary (lint-enforced). Build one for content
  you have rights to.
- [bench/README.md](bench/README.md): the rules-fidelity benchmark — score any
  model or agent (`cmd:` driver reads stdin) against SRD-cited gold verdicts;
  published findings: frontier models ace rules knowledge and fail by false
  confidence exactly where the rules end.

srdcheck is unofficial and not affiliated with or endorsed by Wizards of the
Coast. Rule content derives solely from the SRD 5.2.1 under CC-BY-4.0, pinned
by SHA-256 and rebuilt in CI.
